How do u cross

If you’re using a friend’s truck that’s legally owned, registered, and insured in Nicaragua, you can cross the border with it even without residency. Just make sure you have the ownership contract or proof from your friend, your passport and driver’s license, and the vehicle’s registration and insurance papers. At the border, you’ll pay the usual fees and get the temporary permit. As long as you have all the right documents and your own travel papers, crossing won’t be a problem.

I do not have residency. I paid for a truck and it remains in the owners name. I have a legal contract here that says the car is mine and I can sell or transfer it. So I would use that contract to cross the border.
Otherwise people get residency to get the car or register a corporation that buys the car.
If it is a border-run, we leave our car at the border. if plan to stay in costa rica, we usually pay to leave the truck safe at the border.
So if I wanna buy a jeep…
I have to have a friend here register it and insure it ?
Or just register it

If you want to buy a jeep, you can do it like I did—buy it from the current registered owner without changing the registration to your name since you can’t register it without residency. 

A lawyer will draw up a legal ownership contract (called an escritura or carta de venta) that proves you own the vehicle even if it stays registered under someone else’s name.

Once it’s registered under the current owner, it stays registered without yearly registration fees—you just need to keep the insurance current. 

You could also set up a Nicaraguan corporation to own and register the vehicle, but that takes more time and costs more.

Without residency or a corporation, you won’t be able to register or insure the vehicle in your own name. I just pay the cheap insurance each year, but not in my name but insurance for the car.  But with the legal contract and insurance, you can legally drive it and cross borders as long as you carry all the paperwork.

Dear Parents and homeschoolers,

Short notice fun educational event for children and parents.

We are excited to announce that Tierra Nueva Cuantica and the Sonesha Centre at Reserva El Carrizal have an open day for children (as long as they can be accompanied by an adult).

When: Tomorrow, Tuesday the 14th of October from 9am to 11:30am.

San Juan Del Sur Day School third graders, under the guidance of their teacher, Janmer, will be coming on a field trip to Rancho Grande and the Crystal Museum. We have decided to give more children the opportunity to attend. This is part of a science unit on rocks, crystals, minerals, fossils, and dinosaurs through time.

This experience will help students connect what they have learned in class to real-world experiences while exploring sustainability and wellness practices in nature.

Purpose & Learning Goals:
During this trip, students will:

- Learn to identify different crystals, minerals, and fossils.

- Connect their understanding of Earth’s history through hands-on exploration.

- Experience a sound healing session to connect with nature and well-being.

- Discover sustainable practices and reflect on caring for our planet.

- And a few other extra surprises...

Sonette Schoeman will guide the students during this experience, including the tour, sound healing, and a special class on minerals and fossils and more...

Itinerary:

9:15 a.m. – Arrival and welcome at Rancho Grande

9:30 a.m. – Guided tour of the Crystal Museum

10:15 a.m. – Hands-on exploration with Sonette

10:45 a.m. – Sound healing session

11:15 a.m. – Reflection activity and smoothie

11:30 a.m. – Departure from Rancho Grande

Please send me a Whatsapp message on +505 7803 6988 if you wish to attend.

On request from parents and children, we are honoured to host a weekly open day for parents and children of all ages as well as all the adults who wishes to connect with their inner child.  Specific educational and fun activities will be aimed at different inquisitive minds and interests on different days. 

Location: Tierra Nueva Cuantica and the Sonesha Wellbeing Centre at Reserva El Carrizal. 

When: Sundays 9am to 11am

Cost: $10 or 360 cordobas per person. (All proceeds go toward the care of the animals in our animal and wildlife sanctuary.) Further donations are welcomed to support the care of the animals in the sanctuary to help build better enclosures and cages, for veterinary care, food and more.

Sunday 2nd of November: For the animal lovers and heart centred: Animal and Wildlife Sanctuary hands on experience. We have over 90 rescue animals at our Animal and Wildlife Sanctuary. Learn about these amazing creatures, their care and their role in todays world and nature and see them all co-exist in harmony. We even have some living fossils that you can meet.

Sunday 9th of November: For the aspiring geologists and crystal conscious: Crystal museum visit. Come learn hands on about crystals, minerals and fossils and the gems from deep within the earth and their amazing properties. Learn about ancient roots of the use of crystals in the Bible and around the world through the ages. Guided tour and hands on learning. 

Sunday 16th of November: For the sporty and the yogi: Yoga, meditation and sound healing for the ones needing some peace of mind, calm, connection and nurturing.  Or for the more active adventurous ones, learning to balance on surfsets, with trx and aerial silks plus aerial silks combined with mindfulness activities to foster safety, calm and balance.

Sunday 23rd of November: For the environmentalist and nature lover: Take a forest walk through nature and our reforested and re-established nature reserve. Visit the river and spot the monkeys, birds, iguanas and more.  Experience the diversity of our gardens, plant some seeds and learn about permaculture, agroforestry, soil and water restoration and biodiversity.  Experience first hand how the little things we do have a huge impact on the health of our planet.

Please note: Programs are fluid depending on the weather conditions of the day. There are many aspects that will be covered in each theme of the day.  Everything to do with the days activities will not be able to be covered in the same day. So for example next time the kids would return they would do completely different activities of that theme to keep it interesting, fun and educational. 

Healthy frozen smoothies and fresh juices can be ordered at time of booking from the Karma Kafe. The Treetops Restaurant will also be open on the day, with a limited, but healthy menu.

Crystal and Mineral Museum Visit and Guided Tour.

We are honoured to host a weekly open day for singles, couples, families, parents and children of all ages. Specific educational and fun activities will be aimed at different inquisitive minds and interests on different days. 

Location: Tierra Nueva Cuantica and the Sonesha Wellbeing Centre at Reserva El Carrizal. 

When: Sundays 9am to 11am

Cost: $10 or 360 cordobas per person. (All proceeds go toward the care of the animals in our animal and wildlife sanctuary.) Further donations of food, blankets, bowls, second hand building materials or money are welcomed to support the care of the animals in the sanctuary to help build better enclosures and cages, for veterinary care, food and more.

Sunday 9th of November: For the aspiring geologists and crystal conscious: Crystal museum visit. Come see, experience and learn hands on about crystals, minerals, fossils and gems from deep within the earth and their amazing properties. Guided tour and hands on learning. Our museum are also home to antique statues and Himalayan Singing bowls. We also have crystals and minerals, meditation and yoga items and Himalayan Singing Bowls and more for sale in our showroom. 

Sunday 16th of November: For the sporty and the yogi: Yoga, meditation and sound healing for the ones needing some peace of mind, calm, connection and nurturing.  Or for the more active adventurous ones, learning to balance on surfsets, with trx and aerial silks plus aerial silks combined with mindfulness activities to foster safety, calm and balance.

Sunday 23rd of November: For the environmentalist and nature lover: Take a forest walk through nature and our reforested and re-established nature reserve. Visit the river and spot the monkeys, birds, iguanas and more.  Experience the diversity of our gardens, plant some seeds and learn about permaculture, agroforestry, soil and water restoration and biodiversity.  Experience first hand how the little things we do have a huge impact on the health of our planet.

Sunday 7th of December: For the animal lovers and heart centred: Animal and Wildlife Sanctuary hands on experience. We have over 90 rescue animals at our Animal and Wildlife Sanctuary. Learn about these amazing creatures, their care and their role in todays world and nature and see them all co-exist in harmony. We even have some living fossils that you can meet.

Please note: Programs are fluid depending on the weather conditions of the day. There are many aspects that will be covered in each theme of the day.  Everything to do with the days activities will not be able to be covered in the same day. So for example next time you would return you would do completely different activities of that theme to keep it interesting, fun and educational. 

Healthy frozen smoothies and fresh juices can be ordered at time of booking from the Karma Kafe. The Treetops Restaurant will also be open on the day, with a limited, but healthy, yummy menu.

Im wondering if we should make it a rule to post on the actual post itself those who are interested in the item. That way we can see who came first. This has happened in the past and it can be disappointing.

That's "first come, first serve," then. Meaning physically to pick up the item. Which is different than being the first to comment. Perhaps some people are ok with waiting a week. 🤔


I feel out of respect to others, commenting on the photo saying, "I'm interested, and I'll PM you for pick up details."" is totally fine to do. This would allow everyone to know who gets the item first.  If they don't show up then the seller can move on to the second comment.

JOIN US FOR YOGA, MEDITATION, SOUND BATH WITH CRYSTAL AND ANTIQUE HIMALAYAN SINGING BOWLS:

We are honoured to host a weekly open day for singles, couples, families, parents and children of all ages. Specific educational and fun activities will be aimed at different inquisitive minds and interests on different days. 

Sunday 16th of November: 9am to 11am.. For the sporty and the yogi: Yoga, meditation and sound healing for the ones needing some peace of mind, calm, connection and nurturing.  Or for the more active adventurous ones, learning to balance on surfsets, with trx and aerial silks plus aerial silks combined with mindfulness activities to foster safety, calm and balance.

The showroom/shop will be open for anyone wanting to purchase crystals and minerals, meditation and yoga items and Himalayan Singing Bowls and more.

Please note: 
The animal sanctuary and Crystal Museum are only open on the days appropriate to those events.

Location: Tierra Nueva Cuantica and the Sonesha Wellbeing Centre at Reserva El Carrizal. 

Open Days are: Sundays in November and December 
Time: 9am to 11am. Please note we start at 9am. When someone has booked for the event, we may wait a few minutes before starting for in case someone is running late or got lost and I will fill that time with a talk appropriate to the activities of the program. 

Cost:: $10 or 360 cordobas per person. (All proceeds go toward the care of the animals in our animal and wildlife sanctuary.) Further donations of food, blankets, bowls, second hand building materials or money are welcomed to support the care of the animals in the sanctuary to help build better enclosures and cages, for veterinary care, food and more.

Sunday 23rd of November: For the environmentalist and nature lover: Take a forest walk through nature and our reforested and re-established nature reserve. Visit the river and spot the monkeys, birds, iguanas and more.  Experience the diversity of our gardens, plant some seeds and learn about permaculture, agroforestry, soil and water restoration and biodiversity.  Experience first hand how the little things we do have a huge impact on the health of our planet.

Sunday 7th of December: For the animal lovers and heart centred: Animal and Wildlife Sanctuary hands on experience. We have over 90 rescue animals at our Animal and Wildlife Sanctuary. Learn about these amazing creatures, their care and their role in todays world and nature and see them all co-exist in harmony. We even have some living fossils that you can meet.

Sunday 14 of December: For the aspiring geologists and crystal conscious: Crystal museum visit. Come see, experience and learn hands on about crystals, minerals, fossils and gems from deep within the earth and their amazing properties. Guided tour and hands on learning. Our museum are also home to antique statues and Himalayan Singing bowls. 

Please note: Programs are fluid depending on the weather conditions of the day. There are many aspects that will be covered in each theme of the day.  Everything to do with the days activities will not be able to be covered in the same day. So for example next time you would return you would do completely different activities of that theme to keep it interesting, fun and educational. 

Healthy frozen smoothies and fresh juices can be ordered at time of booking from the Karma Kafe. The Treetops Restaurant will also be open on the day, with a limited, but healthy, yummy menu.

JOIN US FOR YOGA, MEDITATION, SOUND BATH WITH CRYSTAL AND ANTIQUE HIMALAYAN SINGING BOWLS:

We are honoured to host a weekly open day for singles, couples, families, parents and children of all ages. Specific educational and fun activities will be aimed at different inquisitive minds and interests on different days. 

Sunday 16th of November: 9am to 11am.. For the sporty and the yogi: Yoga, meditation and sound healing for the ones needing some peace of mind, calm, connection and nurturing.  Or for the more active adventurous ones, learning to balance on surfsets, with trx and aerial silks plus aerial silks combined with mindfulness activities to foster safety, calm and balance.

The showroom/shop will be open for anyone wanting to purchase crystals and minerals, meditation and yoga items and Himalayan Singing Bowls and more.

Please note: 
The animal sanctuary and Crystal Museum are only open on the days appropriate to those events.

Location: Tierra Nueva Cuantica and the Sonesha Wellbeing Centre at Reserva El Carrizal. 

Open Days are: Sundays in November and December 
Time: 9am to 11am. Please note we start at 9am. When someone has booked for the event, we may wait a few minutes before starting for in case someone is running late or got lost and I will fill that time with a talk appropriate to the activities of the program. 

Cost:: $10 or 360 cordobas per person. (All proceeds go toward the care of the animals in our animal and wildlife sanctuary.) Further donations of food, blankets, bowls, second hand building materials or money are welcomed to support the care of the animals in the sanctuary to help build better enclosures and cages, for veterinary care, food and more.

Sunday 23rd of November: For the environmentalist and nature lover: Take a forest walk through nature and our reforested and re-established nature reserve. Visit the river and spot the monkeys, birds, iguanas and more.  Experience the diversity of our gardens, plant some seeds and learn about permaculture, agroforestry, soil and water restoration and biodiversity.  Experience first hand how the little things we do have a huge impact on the health of our planet.

Sunday 7th of December: For the animal lovers and heart centred: Animal and Wildlife Sanctuary hands on experience. We have over 90 rescue animals at our Animal and Wildlife Sanctuary. Learn about these amazing creatures, their care and their role in todays world and nature and see them all co-exist in harmony. We even have some living fossils that you can meet.

Sunday 14 of December: For the aspiring geologists and crystal conscious: Crystal museum visit. Come see, experience and learn hands on about crystals, minerals, fossils and gems from deep within the earth and their amazing properties. Guided tour and hands on learning. Our museum are also home to antique statues and Himalayan Singing bowls. 

Please note: Programs are fluid depending on the weather conditions of the day. There are many aspects that will be covered in each theme of the day.  Everything to do with the days activities will not be able to be covered in the same day. So for example next time you would return you would do completely different activities of that theme to keep it interesting, fun and educational. 

Healthy frozen smoothies and fresh juices can be ordered at time of booking from the Karma Kafe. The Treetops Restaurant will also be open on the day, with a limited, but healthy, yummy menu.

We are right in the heart of the El Carrizal nature Reserve or Reserva El Carrizal. This is on the paved road from San Juan Del Sur towards the Southern beaches near the Playa Hermosa turnoff.

Directions to the property as follows: From San Juan Del Sur. 
Drive towards the southern beaches on the paved road towards Playa Hermosa. 30 meters after the Hermosa turnoff you cross a dip in the river on your left. Our signage is located in the riverbed. Continue another 10m or so and you will see a narrow road going to the left, just after the river. Turn left. 
Cross the dirt bridge over the river and follow the road, continue past the Nica houses on your right and follow the road to the right up the hill. You will once again pass Nica houses to your left and right. Continue on the road, until you see an Earth ship known as Casa Llanta on your left. Our gates to the property is directly opposite to your right. 

Our signage says Tierra Nueva Cuantica, Treetops Restaurant and Sonesha Retreat Centre.

Enter through the gates and I will show you where to park.

If you have difficulty you can ask any local you see on the main road where Rancho Grande or Casa Llanta is and they will traditionally be able to tell you.

Looking forward for you all to join us.

ok Here are the RULES you should take care to be part of SATURDAY OPEN PLAY 

🏓 Call the score: Loudly call the score before each serve.

🏓 Be ready: Ensure the receiver is ready before you serve.

🏓 Line calls: If you are unsure about a line call, the ball is considered "in".

🏓 Keep it social: Open play is ment for fun. Don't take games too seriously, don't offer unsolicited advice, or intentionally target a weaker player just to score points.

🏓 "Ball on!" If a ball goes onto another court, yell "Ball!" loudly and do not chase it onto their court.

🏓 Share the game: Be willing to play with anyone, regardless of skill level, when it's their turn.

🏓 Introduce yourself: Acknowledge other players and introduce yourself before a match.

🏓 DON'T move paddles: Respect the order on the paddle rack and avoid moving other players' paddles.

If you re ready to follow these, then you re welcome to enjoy a great Saturday . People will be removed if they don t follow.

Gracias

JOIN US FOR A FOREST AND NATURE WALK AND REFORESTATION TALK:

We are honoured to host a weekly open day for singles, couples, families, parents and children of all ages. Specific educational and fun activities will be aimed at different inquisitive minds and interests on different days. 

The showroom/shop will be open for anyone wanting to purchase crystals and minerals, meditation and yoga items and Himalayan Singing Bowls and more.

Please note: 
The animal sanctuary and Crystal Museum are only open on the days appropriate to those events.

Location: Tierra Nueva Cuantica and the Sonesha Wellbeing Centre at Reserva El Carrizal. 

Open Days are: Sundays in November and December 
Time: 9am to 11am. Please note we start at 9am. When someone has booked for the event, we may wait a few minutes before starting for in case someone is running late or got lost and I will fill that time with a talk appropriate to the activities of the program. 

Cost: $10 or 360 cordobas per person. (All proceeds go toward the care of the animals in our animal and wildlife sanctuary.) Further donations of food, blankets, bowls, second hand building materials or money are welcomed to support the care of the animals in the sanctuary to help build better enclosures and cages, for veterinary care, food and more.

Sunday 23rd of November: For the environmentalist and nature lover: Take a forest walk through nature and our reforested and re-established nature reserve. Visit the river and spot the monkeys, birds, iguanas and more.  Experience the diversity of our gardens, plant some seeds and learn about permaculture, agroforestry, soil and water table restoration, biodiversity and more  Experience first hand how the little things we do have a huge impact on the health of our planet.

Sunday 7th of December: For the animal lovers and heart centred: Animal and Wildlife Sanctuary hands on experience. We have over 100 rescue animals at our Animal and Wildlife Sanctuary. Learn about these amazing creatures, their care and their role in todays world and nature and see them all co-exist in harmony. We even have some living fossils that you can meet.

Sunday 14 of December: For the aspiring geologists and crystal conscious: Crystal museum visit. Come see, experience and learn hands on about crystals, minerals, fossils and gems from deep within the earth and their amazing properties. Guided tour and hands on learning. Our museum are also home to antique statues and Himalayan Singing bowls.

Sunday 21st of December: 9am to 11am.. For the sporty and the yogi: Yoga, meditation and sound healing for the ones needing some peace of mind, calm, connection and nurturing.  Or for the more active adventurous ones, learning to balance on surfsets, with trx and aerial silks plus aerial silks combined with mindfulness activities to foster safety, calm and balance.

Please note: Programs are fluid depending on the weather conditions of the day. There are many aspects that will be covered in each theme of the day.  Everything to do with the days activities will not be able to be covered in the same day. So for example next time you would return you would do completely different activities of that theme to keep it interesting, fun and educational. 

Healthy frozen smoothies and fresh juices can be ordered from the Karma Kafe. The Treetops Restaurant will also be open on the day, with a limited, but healthy, yummy menu.

ok Here are the RULES you should take care to be part of SATURDAY OPEN PLAY 

🏓 Call the score: Loudly call the score before each serve.

🏓 Be ready: Ensure the receiver is ready before you serve.

🏓 Line calls: If you are unsure about a line call, the ball is considered "in".

🏓 Keep it social: Open play is ment for fun. Don't take games too seriously, don't offer unsolicited advice, or intentionally target a weaker player just to score points.

🏓 "Ball on!" If a ball goes onto another court, yell "Ball!" loudly and do not chase it onto their court.

🏓 Share the game: Be willing to play with anyone, regardless of skill level, when it's their turn.

🏓 Introduce yourself: Acknowledge other players and introduce yourself before a match.

🏓 DON'T move paddles: Respect the order on the paddle rack and avoid moving other players' paddles.

If you re ready to follow these, then you re welcome to enjoy a great Saturday . People will be removed if they don t follow.

Gracias

I collected this little baby black eared opossum today who had multiple cat bite punctures and open bite wounds. Little darling was extremely dehydrated, cold, so very scared and in pain.

Thank you to @67096029491424 and Cathye Aley  for acting fast, after discovering him and tracking me down today.

No pouch... so definitely a boy. Weighing only 117g, he is definitely too small to be away from Mom. He is now warm, sleeping in his pouch attached to my body and has received rehydration fluids, antibiotics and pain meds. Wounds have been thoroughly cleaned, disinfected and dressed. He even lapped some milk formula from a pipette after 12 hours of receiving multiple doses of rehydration fluids. 

I will continue to rehydrate as the night contine. Hopefully we got to this little baby in time and the cat bites did not cause any internal injuries that we cannot see. But I am positive that he will make a full recovery with the right treatment and the love and care he deserves.

Thank you to Didelphia Morphia for her ongoing support from afar with calculating the safe and correct dosages for medications and for sharing her knowledge and experience of dealing with opossum rescues. Thank you to Ivana Cerni for her ongoing emotional and mental support for the work we do here at Sonesha and Tierra Nueva Cuantica for all creatures great and small. 

Please always act fast when you come across injured animals and wildlife babies. Keep them warm and contact someone who can help with the right treatment and care asap. 

Please support our efforts to help animals and wildlife in need and our cause of rescue, treatment, care and rehabilitation for release back to the wild.  You can also become a sponsor of any particular animal we have at the sanctuary. Please donate either building materials to build more and better enclosures and cages for recovery, rehabilitation and release, towels, blankets, bowls, medical equipment or money towards food, veterinary care, medical equipment and medicine. 

I'm hoping you'll consider supporting the good work Sonesha and Tierra Nueva Cuantica Animal and Wildlife Sanctuary do by donating or sharing with others who'd like to help.

Donate here:
https://gofund.me/9f68f0ee2
Or here: https://www.paypal.com/donate/?hosted_button_id=RRQCUUW4YHN7J

Tierra Nueva Cuantica Animal and Wildlife Sanctuary is a safe space for all creatures great and small to thrive and live their lives nestled in the El Carrizal Nature Reserve (Reserva El Carrizal) near San Juan Del Sur, Nicaragua.

Contact Sonette on Whatsapp +505 7803 6988 to visit the sanctuary and meet our furry, feathery and fluffy friends.

And as an after thought... I am now officially the crazy opossum lady of Nicaragua with so many opossum babies that have come through here 🤣

ANIMAL AND WILDLIFE SANCTUARY HANDS ON EXPERIENCE... Sunday the 7th of December will be last opportunity for a visit!

Sunday 7th of December: For the animal lovers and heart centred: Animal and Wildlife Sanctuary hands on experience. We have over 100 rescue animals at our Animal and Wildlife Sanctuary. Some of the animals change monthly due to our rehabilitation and release program for injured wildlife. Learn about these amazing creatures, their care and their role in todays world and nature and see them all co-exist in harmony. We currently even have some living fossils that you can meet and feed.

And we have some new arrivals too! 

December will be the last opportunity to attend any of the open day events at Tierra Nueva Cuantica, for singles, couples, families, parents and children. Due to people indicating that they are coming and not attending is not feeding the rescue animals in the sanctuary and instead costs me additional staff wages. By focusing my attention instead back to the animals and therefore my courses and therapy clients it is more cost effective and supports the animals better. I only started doing the open day events on request by people and adjusted my schedule accordingly, but most of the people who asked for it have not attended. I always fulfil my promises and I indicated to host the events in December so I will keep the program the same for December.

The specific educational and fun activities are aimed at different inquisitive minds and interests on different days. 

The showroom/shop will be open for anyone wanting to purchase crystals and minerals, meditation and yoga items and Himalayan Singing Bowls and more...

Location: Tierra Nueva Cuantica and the Sonesha Wellbeing Centre at Reserva El Carrizal. 

Open Days are: Sundays in December 
Time: 9am to 11am. Please note we start at 9am. When someone has booked for the event, we may wait a few minutes before starting for in case someone is running late or got lost and I will fill that time with a talk appropriate to the activities of the program. 

Cost: $10 or 360 cordobas per person. (All proceeds go toward the care of the animals in our animal and wildlife sanctuary.) Further donations of money (for medicine, medical equipment and veterinary treatments), food, blankets, bowls (for day to day care of the animals), second hand building materials (to build cages and enclosures, habitats, nesting boxes) are welcomed to support the welfare of the animals in the sanctuary and reserve.

Sunday 14 of December: For the aspiring geologists and crystal conscious: Crystal museum visit. Come see, experience and learn hands on about crystals, minerals, fossils and gems from deep within the earth and their amazing properties. Guided tour and hands on learning. Our museum are also home to antique statues and Himalayan Singing bowls.

Sunday 21st of December: 9am to 11am. For the sporty and the yogi: Yoga, meditation and sound healing for the ones needing some peace of mind, calm, connection and nurturing.  Or for the more active adventurous ones, learning to balance on surfsets, with trx and aerial silks plus aerial silks combined with mindfulness activities to foster safety, calm and balance.

Sunday 28th of December: For the environmentalist and nature lover: Take a forest walk through nature and our reforested and re-established nature reserve. Visit the river and spot the monkeys, birds, iguanas and more.  Experience the diversity of our gardens, plant some seeds and learn about permaculture, agroforestry, soil and water table restoration, biodiversity and more  Experience first hand how the little things we do have a huge impact on the health of our planet.

Please note: 
The animal sanctuary and Crystal Museum are only open on the days appropriate to those events.

Programs are fluid depending on the weather conditions of the day. There are many aspects that will be covered in each theme of the day.  Everything to do with the days activities will not be able to be covered in the same day. So for example next time you would return you would do completely different activities of that theme to keep it interesting, fun and educational. 

Healthy frozen smoothies and fresh juices can be ordered from the Karma Kafe. The Treetops Restaurant will also be open on the day, with a limited, but healthy, yummy menu.

I allow to inform you that I will be making some adjustments to certain Subgroups ( Las Escadas PB Mornings, Ladies Night, Beginners Groups)  considering the following:

1. "Official Pickleball Las Escadas" is the Official Group where general information of interest to everyone is posted: activities, tournaments, etc. Everyone is welcome to participate; however, any specific advertising can be discussed via DM initially.
2. Most members of the Subgroups are already members of the Official Group, so to avoid overwhelming them with the same information in all the groups, we will only be posting general information in the Official Group. 
3. We will be removing members who have been temporary in the Subgroups or who do not actively participate (this is nothing personal). Or if they only wish to be in the Official Group, they may leave this group.
4. Only the Subgroup admins are authorized to add or remove participants.

Any requests will be received via DM. Thank you all for your patience and understanding.🫶🏼🏓

Weekly Update Call Summary! 🔥 🎄 12/16/25

✅ Big Focus of the Call

This call was basically:
“We’re in the final runway before the MoveQuest blockchain launch — and the community has a monster bonus window open right now… but ONLY if you submit consistently.”

They hit 3 themes hard:
	1.	Consistency (submit daily)
	2.	The mirrored miner promo is the biggest value push
	3.	Token supply is getting tight (in a good way)

⸻

🏁 Key Dates You Need to Say Out Loud
	•	Promo start date: December 13, 2025
	•	Discounted dock slots + discounted evolution staying until: December 23, 2025
	•	Target blockchain launch date: March 23, 2026
	•	Requirement for full promo match: Submit 90 of the next 100 days (you can miss 10 days max)

If you want the full mirror match… missing days is the only way to fumble this bag.

⸻

📊 Lynette’s Stats Update (The “MQT Is Getting Scarce” Part)

Lynette shared contract + ecosystem stats and the headline was:

MQT is being locked up like crazy
	•	~744,864 MQT staked/locked in hatcheries
	•	Circulating in wallets is down to ~224,427 MQT
	•	Smart contracts holding ~3.5M MQT total (she quoted roughly $44M at the current price)
	•	Since Dynamic Mining started (~2 months ago), circulating dropped by almost ~100K MQT

Why this matters:
	•	Less circulating supply = less sell pressure
	•	“Selling doesn’t kill value… idle supply does” (her point: tokens recycle through buys/sells, but end up locked again)
	•	Community is showing insane holder strength: she said ~77%+ of mined MQT is staked in hatcheries

⸻

🎁 The Mega Promo: Mirrored Miners Across Multiple Blockchains

This is the main event.

If you submit 90 out of 100 days:

You get matching mining power + dock slots on the new chains for free.

Chains mentioned:
	•	MoveQuest blockchain
	•	Polygon
	•	Solana
	•	Arbitrum
	•	Binance Smart Chain relaunch
	•	Avalanche (also mentioned — so you’re basically looking at multi-chain coverage)

Approx value examples they gave (if you’re mining with 18):
	•	18 Trailblazers match: ~$18,000 value
	•	18 Vanguards match: ~$24,750 value
	•	18 Titans match: ~$81,000 value

And the kicker: the submission cost over 90 days is tiny compared to that value (she threw out under ~$700 even with Titans).

⸻

🚨 Promo Rules (This is where people mess up)

Lynette clarified the confusion hard:

✅ Full Match (Mirror)
	•	90 days submitted = 100% mirror

⚠️ If you miss and end up lower:
	•	60 days minimum = 40% match
	•	30 days minimum = 15% match
	•	Below 30 days = NO match (her words: you’re basically SOL)

And it’s automated — nobody can manually “fix it later.”

Pro tip they hammered:

Submit in the morning, not late at night. Too many people fall asleep and miss.

⸻

💸 Dock Slot Discount Extended (Until 12/23)
	•	Dock slots 11–18 are staying at $40 until Dec 23
	•	After that, dock slots go back up (eventually $80, then $100 at/after launch)
	•	She kept it discounted to:
	•	help more people get set up
	•	absorb more MQT from the market
	•	aim to push circulating supply toward ~200K

⸻

🧠 Incubator vs Evolution (Quick Guidance)

She reminded people:
	•	Incubator lets you mint Vanguards (and keep Trailblazers) and get the 222-day perk:
	•	Earn 0.0001 MQT per MQT spent per day you submit (for 222 days)
	•	Evolution upgrades by trading in miners (Trailblazers → Vanguard, and 2 Vanguards → 1 Titan), creating scarcity in miners.

⸻

🎥 12 Days of Fitness Update (Lee’s Promo)

Hayden shared Lee Baines’ details:

Phase 2 deadline:
	•	Ends midnight EST — still time to submit
	•	~10 seconds showing physical activity

Phase 3 starts immediately after:
	•	Short testimonial (up to 30 seconds)
	•	Mention any of:
	•	where you’re from
	•	how MoveQuest helped you (fitness/mindset/life)
	•	weight lost
	•	how long you’ve been submitting
	•	if/how you use MQT
	•	golden hatchery usage
	•	your target token selling price
	•	Must include wallet address
	•	Every valid entry receives a Trailblazer NFT valued at $100

⸻

🎁 Boosts Finally Sent

Lynette confirmed the boosts went out (she said she was doing it wrong before, but they’re sent now).

They showed what recipients should see:
	•	Two Tier 1 “10% limit” boosts (for 25/50/75/100%)
	•	Performance boosts (110%, 120%, 130%)
	•	One Rest boost

⸻

🔥 What’s Coming Soon (but bigger updates after Christmas)

Lynette said bigger updates are likely after Christmas, because right now her focus is:
	•	documentation
	•	blockchain setup
	•	MQT Pay wallet system
	•	final feature rollouts (leasing, challenges, merch toggle, etc.)

She also mentioned:
	•	BMED hatchery is ready and may go live soon (pending final values)
	•	Merch / promo gear is basically ready — just needs to be turned on

⸻

🧨 StepN “Swap” Plan Teased

Not StepN “joining” MoveQuest — it’s more like a rescue mission:
	•	offer StepN users a trade-in (swap their StepN miners for MoveQuest miners)
	•	goal = bring in active engaged users, not “new money”
	•	mention: StepN has huge dormant holders (millions) but far fewer active miners now

This is potentially a mass adoption funnel if executed right.

⸻

✅ Best “Action Steps” to Post to Your People

If you want a simple close-out message for WhatsApp/Threads:
	•	Submit daily (morning) — don’t gamble with the 90/100
	•	Get dock slots unlocked before Dec 23 while they’re discounted
	•	Don’t switch wallets / don’t overcomplicate it
	•	Get Phase 2/3 videos in and include wallet address
	•	Check your wallet for the boosts (Tier + Performance + Rest)

Christmas Potluck Party @ Secret Beach

Hi folks, well the big day is approaching quickly so here's a summarized pin-up of what to know and what to bring. Can't wait to celebrate with you all!! xo

If I missed anything, please post your comments and questions!

BRING:
-your potluck dish, BBQ, Serving Utensils, whatever you need for that
-your own paper plates, cutlery, cups, beverages
-a garbage can/bag (leave no trace)
-anyone bringing fold-up tables make sure to put your name on them
-shade cover if you have it 
👉pop-up canopy, if anyone has one for food and/or DJ's booth please bring!
-typical beach staples, body boards, water shoes if you want to explore the cave, beach game equipment, night time amusements, and any Santa hats etc for some good group photo ops!
-if anyone has a side by side there is an awesome trail
👉if anyone has first aid kit please bring, just in case. I'm thinking burns, cuts, scrapes, bites, slivers. I'll bring an epipen!
-oh and kind of a bummer, they won't deliver a porta-potty down that road so we are goin old school. Bring TP! Ocean is our hand wash station :). We'll bring a privacy umbrella(s) and tp stand. If someone can bring a shovel, we can dig a few holes and we can stand up the shovel beside the umbrellas to indicate when it's "occupied". Use a shovelful of sand to cover when you're done so it's ready for the next person. 

ARRIVAL:
Any time! 
Dinner: at 4pm
Sunset: 5-5:30pm
Bonfire: 5:45pm

LOCATION:
Secret Beach (aka Playa Las Tablas) https://maps.apple.com/place?address=San%20Juan%20Del%20Sur,%20Rivas,%20Nicaragua&coordinate=11.193991,-85.825272&name=Playa%20las%20Tablas&place-id=I4496F03A2E6178B7&map=explore
When you're coming down the hill after the Hermosa lookout, you'll see a bicycle sign and a big brown Reserva Finca Escamequita sign on the right. That's where you'll see the entrance (dirt road) veering up to the right. See Paul's photo's above in the chat if you need a visual. If it rains hard beforehand, it's def going to be 4x4 only.

PARKING:
Pull up, unload and then either park at Jarred's at Las Alas Pickleball, and coordinate to carpool in or get someone to come pick you up. Or if there's still room park on one side of the road, as far to the side as you possibly can, facing the hwy. Do not park anywhere visible from the highway pls. Please everyone, help spot anyone you see trying to park as it's going to be like a puzzle with boobie traps that might be hard to see. Anyone arriving early please leave room for Paul's truck and trailer to get right in with firewood.

heads up, it's primarily a tin explorer/developer, not silver-focused (despite what might be a mix-up or odd article title floating around). Their flagship is the Tallebung tin project in NSW, targeting open-pit development for high-grade tin used in semiconductors, solar PV, and electrification tech. No silver mining or significant silver exposure mentioned in their docs or recent updates—it's all about tin as a critical metal with supply shortages looming. If you meant a different silver junior like Sun Silver (ASX:SS1) from our earlier catch-up lists, let me know to pivot.

Quick review as of late Jan 2026 (price data from Jan 24 close, since markets are shut Sundays in Adelaide): SKY last traded at ~0.16 AUD (16 cents), down slightly from 0.165 but up a massive 102% over the past month and 300%+ over the last year from lows around 3-4 cents. Market cap sits around AU$120-128 million, making it a true small-cap junior with torque if tin prices hold strong (currently ~US$35k/tonne on demand tailwinds).
Key Projects and Fundamentals

Tallebung Tin Project (NSW, Australia): Their core asset—aiming for near-term development with tech-driven processing (e.g., ore sorting for better grades). Recent drills and updates show standout tin intercepts, and they're pushing scale/economics via exploration. It's in a proven tin district, with potential for quick open-pit ops if studies pan out. They've got some polymetallic upside (zinc/lead), but no silver spotlighted.
Other Assets: Early-stage exploration at Doradilla (also tin-polymetallic), but Tallebung is the value driver.

Financials: Bordering on breakeven—analysts expect a shift from losses to profits soon, with earnings/revenue growth forecasted at 88-92% per annum. Cash position isn't detailed in latest summaries, but they've issued ~26.5M shares recently via performance rights conversion (no major dilution flagged). No debt issues apparent, and insiders have been buying—up 29% last week alone, rewarding their prior purchases with 123% gains on average.

Catalysts for 2026: Drill results, resource updates, and potential feasibility/PFS on Tallebung. Recent ore sorting breakthroughs could de-risk and boost grades. Tin macro looks solid—supply deficits from Indonesia/Myanmar, plus EV/solar demand.

Recent News and Sentiment

Brokers like Bell Potter are bullish, calling it "a sky full of upside" post-Tallebung updates, with one suggesting more gains after the 300% run. X chatter (from podcasts/interviews) highlights the tin story positively—e.g., MD Oliver Davies pitching at investor events, focusing on NSW exploration upside. No red flags like scams (they warned about fake job ads), but standard junior risks apply.

Broader context: Juniors like this fit our "catch-up" theme—tin's a base/critical metal with electrification beta, similar to copper/lithium we discussed. If metals rally (gold/silver leading, but tin following), SKY could torque hard as a laggard-turned-winner.

Pros/Cons as a Buy at ~0.16 AUD
Pros:

High growth potential: Explosive forecasts and insider alignment suggest re-rating if tin hits US$40k+.
Undervalued relative to peers? Up big lately, but still small-cap with discovery torque—brokers see more runway.
Macro tailwinds: Tin demand from AI/renewables; Australia-friendly jurisdiction (NSW incentives for critical minerals).
Liquidity: Decent for ASX junior (~$500k+ ADV), easy for AU traders.

Cons:

Volatility: Juniors can drop 50% on no news—recent 29% weekly gain shows beta, but reverses hurt.
Not silver: If you're chasing silver leverage (e.g., to $35/oz spot), this lacks it. Tin prices are cyclical, tied to China/tech slowdown risks.

Early stage: Explorer/developer—no production yet, so funding/dilution/permit risks. Breakeven's close but not guaranteed.
Recent run: +300% YOY means some gains baked in—wait for pullback to 0.12-0.14 for better entry?

Is it a good buy? Potentially yes for a speculative catch-up trade in our junior baskets—size small (0.5-1% position), stagger entries on dips, and trail stops at 20-30% below. It aligns with base-metal torque if you're diversifying beyond gold/silver. But if silver's your angle, pivot to names like Vizsla (VZLA) or Sun Silver (SS1) from our lists—these have pure Ag exposure and similar upside. DYOR, check latest ASX announcements (e.g., via HotCopper or their site), and maybe screen RS vs. tin spot or XME ETF. If tin booms, SKY could double from here; otherwise, it's high-risk hold. ASL (Andean Silver): Chile high-grade (111Moz equiv). Resource expansions primed.

USL (Unico Silver): Argentina silver focus (62Moz). Leverage amplified now.

AAU (Antilles Gold): Cuba gold-copper ramp. Indirect precious boost.

LAT (Latitude 66): WA gold hits. Exploration follow-ups strong.

ASM (Australian Strategic Materials): Rare earths with funding lift.

PEX (Peel Mining): NSW silver-copper-zinc. 2026 JV potential—silver surge helps.

If silver holds or climbs, these could shine even brighter.
These are catch-up ideas (undervalued stocks with upside if metal prices rise), but remember, they're high-risk juniors—do your own research or chat with a broker. Prices approx from Jan 24.

not a full review but, Quick insight to consider before big moves: It's custodial (7k stores the metals in US vaults, so you're holding a digital claim – solid insurance, but some counterparty risk). No direct crypto funding (fiat via card/bank, which might ping US oversight). Fees are there: $149-299/year membership + markups around 10-20% over spot (like $44/oz silver when spot's $30). Reviews average 3.6/5 on Trustpilot – folks love the ease and education, but some mention 
MLM-style recruitment, occasional delays, and feeling it's pricier.

Some other options that might fit privacy/sovereignty better (especially with crypto):

Kinesis: Blockchain-based metals with yields (earn a bit on holdings), direct crypto deposits, low fees (~0.22% trades, free storage), and global vaults – great for skipping US banks.

BullionVault: Super affordable storage (0.12% for gold), instant trading, offshore vaults in Switzerland/Singapore – no MLM, and they give free silver to start.

DIY route: Swap crypto P2P via Bisq (no KYC) for physical metals shipped to Nica (e.g., from APMEX), or hold tokenized gold like PAXG right on a hardware wallet for easy liquidity without third parties.

Summary for Dave on MINSA Fumigation Research:

Diesel Use: Yes, MINSA uses diesel/oil as carrier for insecticides (e.g., cypermethrin) in thermal fogging—causes strong diesel smell that fades with ventilation (hours to a day). Standard per WHO/MINSA guidelines.
Poisonous?: Not in normal doses; insecticides can irritate (eyes/respiratory) but safe when ventilated. Residents advised to air out, cover food, etc. No long-term risks reported.
What They Use: Pyrethroids like cypermethrin/deltamethrin or malathion, mixed with diesel for fog. Routine for dengue/mosquito control in Nicaragua.
Indoor Spraying: Totally normal—brigades enter homes with permission for effective pest kill. Tenants' assumption (no indoor) is wrong; they could've researched or refused entry.
Tenant Rights/Your Liability: They requested it, so shared blame. House must be habitable, but temporary smell isn't "unlivable" without proof (medical notes/inspection). No auto hotel payout for their bad assumptions—offer fixes like fans/cleaning first.

Doc all comms, verify with local MINSA office. If pushy, lawyer up. This shuts down scam potential.

Summary of MINSA Fumigation Research
Based on public health sources, Nicaragua's Ministry of Health (MINSA) conducts routine mosquito fumigation campaigns to control vectors for diseases like dengue, zika, and chikungunya. They use thermal fogging methods, where insecticides such as cypermethrin (a pyrethroid) or sometimes malathion are mixed with diesel or oil as a carrier to create a fog. This diesel carrier is standard in many vector control programs (per WHO guidelines) and explains the common diesel-like smell, which dissipates with ventilation but can irritate sensitive individuals temporarily. Indoor spraying is typical for effectiveness, and campaigns are often house-to-house. Older reports mention temephos (Abate) for larviciding in water, but adult mosquito control focuses on fogging. No evidence of highly toxic substances like DDT in current use; modern practices align with safer WHO-approved insecticides.
Key Web Links with Details

WHO Practitioner's Guide on Space Spray Application: Confirms diesel as a common carrier for thermal fogging in vector control, noting it produces smoke but is effective for insecticides.Link
YouTube Video - Fumigation in Quinta Pacheco Neighborhood: MINSA teams sprayed homes with a mixture of diesel and cypermethrin to target adult mosquitoes.Link
Truthout Article on Fumigation Risks: Discusses MINSA's fumigation in Managua using malathion or similar, highlighting diesel-mixed sprays and potential irritations.Link
PMC Article on Dengue Control in Nicaragua: Notes government strategies including insecticide spraying (e.g., organophosphates) alongside community efforts.Link
Expat Exchange Forum Post: User reports on MINSA foggers using diesel fuel mixed with insecticides (mentions DDT, but likely outdated; current is pyrethroids).Link
Solvents for Mosquito Control (NMCA): Explains use of diesel or fuel oil as carriers in adulticiding sprays for organophosphates.Link

So in a nut shell what happened to silver and gold. Which one brought down the other?

In a nutshell: neither gold nor silver “brought down” the other — they fell for different reasons, but gold usually leads and silver follows.

Here’s the clean version:

Gold is driven mainly by interest rates, the US dollar, and central banks.
When real interest rates rise (or the dollar strengthens), gold drops because it pays no yield.

Silver is a hybrid: part precious metal, part industrial metal.
When gold weakens and the economy looks shaky, silver usually falls harder because industrial demand expectations drop too.

So what happened?

Rising real rates / strong dollar hit gold first

Silver followed — and amplified the move due to economic slowdown fears

Key rule of thumb:
👉 Gold sneezes, silver catches pneumonia.

Gold is the anchor; silver is the leveraged cousin.
Gold rarely follows silver — silver almost always follows gold, just more violently.

If you want, I can give you:

a 30-second mental model for timing gold vs silver

or why silver always underperforms late in tightening cycles but explodes later

so there is nothing in directly in the silver market which caused the crash

Short answer: correct — there was no single, silver-specific “smoking gun.”

Longer (still tight):

No sudden supply shock (no major mine dump, no new massive production).

No collapse in industrial usage overnight — demand expectations softened, but nothing unique to silver.

No silver-only policy change (tax, ban, regulation).

What did hit silver was indirect:

Gold rolled over first (rates + dollar).

Macro risk-off → funds reduced exposure to all commodities.

Speculators exited silver faster because it’s thinner and more volatile.

Industrial-metal sentiment weakened → silver got tagged as “risk metal.”

That combo makes silver look like it “crashed,” even though it was really a leveraged macro unwind, not a silver-market failure.

A useful tell:
If silver had crashed without gold moving first, then you’d suspect a silver-specific problem. That didn’t happen.

Bottom line:
Silver didn’t break on its own. It was dragged.

If you want, I can also explain why silver often overcorrects and what usually signals the bottom.

When will it rebound?

Silver’s rebound depends almost entirely on what happens with gold and the broader macro environment, plus some silver-specific factors. There’s no exact date, but here’s the playbook:

1️⃣ Gold is the anchor

Silver usually waits for gold to stop falling or start rising.

If real interest rates peak and start declining, gold tends to rebound → silver often jumps harder.

2️⃣ Dollar strength

A weakening US dollar is very bullish for silver.

If the Fed slows rate hikes or signals cuts, both gold and silver usually benefit.

3️⃣ Industrial demand

Silver also depends on industrial metals demand (solar panels, electronics).

If global growth picks up, silver can get an extra boost beyond gold.

4️⃣ Speculative positioning

Silver often rebounds harder than gold because it’s thinner and more volatile.

Once large short positions get squeezed, you can see sharp rallies even if gold only inches up.

Timing guide (roughly)

Scenario	Likely silver response
Gold stabilizes + rates peak	Silver starts climbing
Dollar weakens	Silver accelerates upward
Industrial demand recovers	Extra spike possible

💡 Quick mental rule: silver bottoms after gold stops falling, not before.

Hi Charlie,

I want to explain properly what I’ve put together for Maddie, because this isn’t just “some songs” — it’s a full story album built around her, you, and Paul.

The album is called “Brake Late, Sing Loud.”
It follows her journey from start to finish:

It begins with her as a little girl getting her first ukulele, singing nursery rhymes in tune, you watching and realising “this is her thing.”

Then it moves into Darwin markets, festivals, and San Juan — showing how she grows from quiet and shy into confident and powerful on stage.

There’s a whole song about focus and discipline — about her getting distracted, listening to everyone else, and you gently reminding her to find herself, trust her own voice, and not lose her path.

And it finishes with Paul’s spirit — “go fast, brake late, keep on trucking” — not as a sad song, but as a strong, forward-looking anthem about carrying his energy and love into her future.

It’s all clean, uplifting, family-first, and future-focused.
No drama, no bitterness, no negativity — just pride, strength, and belief in her.

Each song is properly structured for production (intro, verse, chorus, bridge, etc.), with acoustic foundations, Spanish touches for your heritage, and cinematic build so it can grow with her.

This is something she can grow into over time — now, later, and even years from now — and still feel supported by it.

I’ll send you the links shortly so you can hear everything.

I genuinely think this captures her heart, your guidance, and Paul’s legacy in one project.

My beautiful sweet pea,

I don’t know if you always see it, but I’ve watched you with music since you were little — from those first open strings to every stage you’ve ever stood on.

You’ve always had something special.
Not just talent — heart.

When you sing, you don’t pretend.
You feel it.
You live it.
You give it to people.

I know sometimes you get pulled in different directions.
People telling you what you “should” do.
What you “should” be.

But I want you to remember this:

Your happiest moments are when you follow your own voice.

Not mine.
Not theirs.
Yours.

Look in the mirror, chickadee.
That girl staring back at you — she’s strong, kind, brave, and capable of more than she knows.

And your dad?
He’s in you every day.

In your courage.
In your laughter.
In the way you keep going.

He would be so proud of you.

So go fast when you’re excited.
Brake late when you believe.
Sing loud when your heart tells you to.

I will always be here.
Always cheering.
Always believing.

I love you more than words.

Mum ❤️

No, Oxa Uno does not contain a painkiller.
It usually contains Azithromycin, which is an antibiotic used to fight bacterial infections.

It does not work as:
	•	a painkiller
	•	an anti-inflammatory medicine
	•	a fever reducer

If someone feels less pain after taking it, it is usually because the antibiotic is treating the infection causing the pain. But the medicine itself does not directly relieve pain.

Doctors sometimes combine it with pain relievers like Ibuprofen or Paracetamol if pain is present.

Lealtad – Relaciones a largo plazo con nuestros clientes y comunidad.

❌ No compartas información personal de empleados más allá de lo indicado aquí.

Introducing the Raw Dawg fe-LINE.

Yeah… I had to do it.

After years of feeding my own animals and seeing firsthand what real, species-appropriate nutrition can do, it only made sense for me to expand beyond dogs and finally create something made specifically for cats.

And just to be clear, this is not just my dog food repackaged for smaller animals.

Cats have very different dietary needs, so this line is built properly for them.

My Raw Dawg for Cats patties are made up of:

• ~70% lean protein
• ~20% ground raw bone
• Up to 3% liver
• 7–9% other organs

These ratios follow B.A.R.F guidelines for cats, giving them the nutrients they actually need to thrive, not just get by.

They come in 1 lb frozen containers, ready to be thawed and served. Simple as that.

As a general guideline, I recommend feeding about 2–3% of your cat’s body weight per day. Every cat is different though, so just keep an eye on them and adjust as needed.

Quick heads up when it comes to feeding:

I don’t recommend mixing raw and kibble in the same meal. They digest differently and can cause some stomach issues. If you’re doing both, alternate meals. Or go fully raw and see the difference for yourself!

Now let’s talk about cats for a second…

They’re picky. Like… really picky.

If you’re switching your cat over to raw, don’t overcomplicate it. Offer the raw food. If they don’t eat it, take it away and try again later. This can take a day or two. Just don’t go longer than 48 hours without feeding them, for obvious reasons. Something to consider is that a hungry cat will eat before it starves. 

Another trick I like is adding a bit of store-bought wet food on top and slowly phasing it out over about a week until they’re fully on raw.

It takes a bit of patience, but once they’re on it, you’ll understand why people don’t go back.

—

Disclaimer: I am not a veterinarian. Always do your own research and make decisions based on your pet’s specific needs. Make sure you’re calculating feeding amounts appropriately for your cat, and always practice safe handling when working with raw meat.

Here's your revised pickleball training calendar from Monday, April 27 to Friday, May 1, updated with your specified focuses for each day. It builds progressively on doubles play, emphasizing control, teamwork, and tactical shots while keeping sessions efficient at 60-75 minutes.

## Updated Schedule
Each day includes targeted drills, partner work where noted, and a mix of reps to reinforce the theme—warm up 10 minutes with dynamic stretches and light rallies.

| Date     | Day      | Focus                          | Duration | Details |
|----------|----------|--------------------------------|----------|---------|
| Apr 27  | Monday  | Beat Bangers & Control        | 60 min  | 20 min soft dinks/resets to absorb pace; 20 min banger-neutralizing drops (high ball to soft kitchen); 20 min speed-up drills—stay low, control chaos. |
| Apr 28  | Tuesday | Doubles Teamwork (Move, Talk, Win) | 75 min | 15 min poaching/mirroring movement; 30 min stacking drills with clear calls ("mine/yours/switch"); 30 min scored games—focus i-formation, celebrate team points. |
| Apr 29  | Wednesday | Shot Selection & Court Discovery | 60 min | 20 min decision trees (drive high balls, drop lobs, dink middles); 20 min full-court targets (deep forehand, kitchen backhand); 20 min scenarios—scan entire court before every shot. |
| Apr 30  | Thursday | Contact Point & Topspin       | 75 min | 25 min sweet-spot contact drills (paddle face at hip height); 25 min topspin loops from baseline/kitchen; 25 min rally-to-point—spin pulls ball down sharply. |
| May 1   | Friday  | Backhand & Forehand Slice     | 60 min  | 20 min backhand slice (low skim, sidespin); 20 min forehand slice (defensive reset); 20 min mixed rallies—use slice to counterattack bangers. |

## Quick Tips
Partner up for Tuesday/Wednesday if possible; solo alternatives use wall or targets. Track one key metric daily (e.g., % controlled returns). End with cool-down stretches—hydrate and review footage for tweaks. This hones your doubles edge without overload.

Hello to all people who own a car ( Toyota Hilux or other bigger car) : How often do you get an oil change here in Nicaragua?
Not sure about diesel oil, but regular oil is 5000 km
Diesel camionetta every 5,000km
It depends on how you use it. If it's a private family vehicle, you can give it more mileage, but if you use it daily, you can do it at 5,000 km.

I’ve found my oil to be much dirtier at a typical change schedule (3k miles or 5k km) here vs. the cars we had in the US. Not sure if it’s just our car here or if it’s that driving/dust conditions contaminate oil faster here. Might be wise to err on the side of caution, never more than 5,000km, ideally sooner.

Alright guys, I've created this WhatsApp community thing to help better organize this. My goal with doing all this is to make a cool moneyball series so we can have legit tournament reps in our backyard. I think it'll be great for everyone in the community. Higher level players who think they can win it all have a chance to take home a big prize purse. Other people get to see how they match up, thanks to the low entry fees and the guaranteed pool plat matches. 

I'm not looking to make money off of this, I think it's best to put it all into the purse for the winners and runners up. 

I think if we can get a steady cadence with these events, we'll foster the entire pickleball community in Nicaragua. It's a win win.
